what's an offer letter?
turns.assistant:
An offer letter is a formal document from an employer to a prospective employee that outlines the key terms of a job offer.

Typically, it includes:
- job title
- salary or pay rate
- start date
- work location or schedule
- benefits
- reporting manager
- any conditions, like background checks or signed agreements

It is often a summary of the offer, not the full employment contract. In some cases it may be non-binding, depending on the employer and local law.

If you want, I can also explain how to read one or what to look for before signing.

turns.user: help me harden our SaaS access
turns.assistant:
Start with identity, then permissions, then audit.

- Enforce MFA everywhere, especially admin and finance roles.
- Remove shared accounts; every user gets a unique identity.
- Use SSO if you have it, and lock admin access behind it.
- Apply least privilege: default-deny, role-based access, no standing broad access.
- Review inactive users and stale tokens weekly.
- Turn on access logs and alert on new admin grants, unusual logins, and mass exports.
- Rotate API keys and revoke anything not actively used.
- Add joiner/mover/leaver controls so access changes with role changes.

If you want, I can turn this into a tighter SaaS access control checklist for your org.
